Hi Samir — thanks, sending a draft with attachments (network_diagram_v2.pdf, isolation_playbook_v1.md). Below are the concise answers to the spreadsheet headings; I'll expand any section you flag in the review.

1) Isolation model (hosted & private) — summary:
- Control plane: logically separated control plane for all hosted customers; optional private control plane for Private deployment (VPC/on-prem). Control plane APIs are served from a hardened management VPC with restricted admin access and audit logging.
- Compute pools: tenant-affinity enforced via allocation tags; hosted customers may share GPU pools only when explicitly configured (shared tenancy) and otherwise run in tenant-isolated pools. Dedicated capacity provides physical isolation.
- Network segmentation: per-tenant VPC subnets + ephemeral tunnel endpoints for private cases. Service sidecars (ingress/egress proxies) sit in the compute tier to terminate customer sessions and enforce token-level ACLs.
- Storage: customer data at rest is compartmentalized using project-scoped object prefixes and encryption keys per-tenant where required. KMS/HSM integration supports customer-managed keys for Private deployments.

2) Egress control & auditing:
- Default hosted mode: egress for inference traffic to model downloads and telemetry is tightly scoped to vendor endpoints; public egress is blocked unless explicitly enabled via allow-lists.
- Private / VPC peered deployments: egress flows through customer-managed NAT/egress gateways and optionally through our bastionless audit relay; we support forced-tunnel configurations and can provide flow logs.
- Auditing: all egress flows are logged (VPC flow logs, proxy logs) and correlated with request IDs; logs are retained per contract (default 90 days, configurable). We provide sha256 checksums for model artifacts and tamper-evident audit trails for model loads.

3) Lateral movement & sidecar compromise mitigations:
- Principle of least privilege across all service accounts and short-lived credentials for internal services.
- Sidecar hardening: sidecars run with minimal Linux capabilities, process sandboxing, and automatic restart with health checks; they perform mutual TLS (mTLS) to backend services.
- KV cache isolation: per-request KV scoping; cache eviction policies and reserved namespaces prevent cross-tenant leakage.
- Network-level controls: microsegmentation with policy enforcement (iptables/ebpf rules) and eBPF-based observability for anomalous flows.
- Incident playbook: automatic model-variant fallback and rollback, ephemeral key revocation, and forensic logs exported to S3 buckets under customer control.

4) Supply-chain / model artifact assurance:
- Artifact signing and provenance: published model hashes and signed manifests; optional reproducible build attestations for custom models.
- Kernel & runtime hardening: signed runtime images, immutable container images for the inference runtime, and scheduled cryptographic integrity checks.

5) Threat model summary (topline):
- External egress exfiltration via compromised sidecar: mitigations include allow-lists, egress proxying, and flow logs.
- Lateral movement from compromised tenant workloads: mitigations include KV namespace isolation, microsegmentation, and rapid credential rotation.
- Control plane compromise: separation of duties, MFA + short-lived admin sessions, and emergency stop (circuit breaker) that isolates workloads.

Attachments: network_diagram_v2.pdf (annotated topology), isolation_playbook_v1.md (detailed controls and runbooks).

If you want, I can annotate the diagram with red/amber/green risk flags for each path. Otherwise, this is ready for your procurement packet.

Regards,
